subject: NeoHoldings private cluster intake — networking, storage & node plan
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@neoholdings.com>

Date: 2027-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NeoHoldings private cluster intake — initial ask

Hi Avery / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. EdgeWorks is our systems integrator and will run the hands-on part, but we wanted to start the intake thread with details so you can size appropriately. High-level constraints:
- Location: Primary site in Phoenix AZ (on-prem colocation) + DR in Austin
- Data residency: US only
- Workloads: inference serving (LLM runtime), small model training for fine-tuning (batch), telemetry + audit logs
- Expected peak qps: ~2k token/sec across 8 concurrent model lanes, spiky in business hours

Questions we want answered now: baseline node mix, recommended storage profile (NVMe local vs network block store), network egress and firewall needs, and any per-tenant isolation recommendations.

Attaching a quick inventory of the racks we expect to provision next week (will follow with real inventory from EdgeWorks): neoholdings-site-inventory.json (attached).

Thanks,
Daniel

Thanks Daniel — good context. Looping Karthik to propose an initial node/storage topology. To help us finalize, please fill the short inventory CSV I attached (preflight-inventory-template.csv) with exact NIC counts, switch uplinks, and whether the racks will be behind a NAT/Gateway or have public egress IPs per-rack. A few clarifying asks below (short bullets):

- Network: Will the site provide a routed /22 for the cluster, or do you plan NAT at the edge? Is BGP available for egress failover?
- HA: Do you require multi-rack pod anti-affinity for all services (strict) or only for critical runtime lanes?
- Storage: Do you have an existing SAN/Isilon/NetApp block service we must use, or do we provision a Ceph/Rook cluster?
- KMS: Will keys be hosted in your KMS (YubiHSM/HSM) or do you want Redwood-managed envelope encryption?
- Compliance: any audit retention windows >2 years?

Proposed next steps: fill the CSV, share network diagram, then schedule a 60-minute technical design session with EdgeWorks + Neo infra team. Karthik — can you draft a node-pool + storage sketch (NVMe local vs shared block tradeoffs) after we get the inventory?

Avery Johnson

Avery — attached the completed inventory and a site egress diagram from EdgeWorks. Quick answers inline:
- Network: Routed /22 available; EdgeWorks will run BGP with two transit peers for failover.
- HA: We want multi-rack anti-affinity for LLM runtime lanes; less strict for batch/aux services.
- Storage: We currently have a NetApp array for general block, but latency-sensitive caches should be local NVMe. No dedicated Ceph today.
- KMS: We have an on-prem HSM (Entrust) and can expose envelope keys via our KMS.
- Retention: Audit logs must be retained 3 years.

See attached: neoholdings-site-inventory.json, phoenix-egress-diagram.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Thanks Daniel — appreciate the completed inventory and the BGP/egress notes. Below is a concise proposal and rationale so we can align before the technical design workshop.

1) Node pool proposal (initial):
- control-plane: 3x m5-like (HA control plane) — 16 vCPU / 64GB — single-rack spread for control availability.
- runtime-small: 8x GPU nodes (A100 equivalent) for low-latency lanes — 8 GPUs distributed across at least 2 racks; prefer local NVMe for KV cache on each node (1.6TB NVMe).
- runtime-large: 2x high-memory GPU nodes for heavy batch/fine-tuning jobs — isolated via taints/tolerations.
- infra: 4x storage/infra nodes — 256GB RAM, 32 vCPU, with 8TB network-attached block for shared PVs.

Rationale: split runtime small/large so we can route low-latency inference to pinned NVMe-backed pods while batch jobs use network block and separate quotas. Distribute GPUs across racks to meet your multi-rack anti-affinity requirement.

2) Storage recommendation:
- Local NVMe on GPU nodes for KV cache and model shards requiring sub-ms access.
- Use your NetApp as primary network block store for long-lived PVs (model artifacts, logs), fronted by a small Rook/Ceph layer if you need dynamic CSI features.
- Encryption: integrate with your Entrust HSM for envelope keys; Redwood will support KMS integration and key usage audit logs.

3) Network and egress:
- Accept routed /22; we recommend dedicated egress subnets per tenant lane for traffic policing.
- Use BGP as EdgeWorks suggested; Redwood routing policies will peer to your egress AS for failover.

4) Operational controls & SLOs:
- Canary rollout for model versions: start 1% of traffic, ramp with automated latency/cost guards.
- KV cache warmup policy recommendations and fallback to network store if local NVMe misses exceed threshold.
- Retention: set audit/log archival to your object store with 3-year lifecycle (we will surface cost impact).

Next steps: if this matches your expectations we will: (a) deliver a short design doc w/ rack-level placement and NIC bonding guidance, (b) produce an installation runbook and canary playbook, (c) schedule the 60-minute technical workshop with EdgeWorks for 2027-03-25.

Attaching a short nodepool-proposal.pdf (sketch) — comments welcome.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Technical PM — Redwood Inference
